The value of $\theta$ for which the system of equations

$\left\left(sin ⁡ 3\theta\right)x - 2y + 3z = 0, ( cos ⁡ 2\theta\right)x + 8y - 7z = 0$~and& $2x + 14y - 11z = 0$ has a non-trivial solution, is (here,~$n \in Z$)
questions.solution:
The system of equations has a non-trivial solution if and only if $\left|\begin{cases}sin ⁡ 3\theta & - 2 & 3 \\ cos ⁡ 2\theta & 8 & - 7 \\ 2 & 14 & - 11\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Applying ${R}_{2} \to {R}_{2} + 4{R}_{1}, {R}_{3} \to {R}_{3} + 7{R}_{1}$, we get,

$\left|\begin{cases}sin ⁡ 3\theta & - 2 & 3 \\ cos ⁡ 2\theta + 4sin ⁡ 3\theta & 0 & 5 \\ 2 + 7sin ⁡ 3\theta & 0 & 10\end{cases}\right| = 0$

Expanding along ${C}_{2}$, we get,

$2\left(cos ⁡ 2\theta + 4sin ⁡ 3\theta\right) - \left(2 + 7sin ⁡ 3\theta\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2 - 2cos ⁡ 2\theta - sin ⁡ 3\theta = 0$

$⇒ 4{sin}^{2} ⁡ \theta - \left(3sin ⁡ \theta - 4{sin}^{3} ⁡ \theta\right) = 0$

$⇒ sin ⁡ \theta\left(4{sin}^{2} ⁡ \theta + 4sin ⁡ \theta - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ sin ⁡ \theta\left(2sin ⁡ \theta - 1\right)\left(2sin ⁡ \theta + 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ sin ⁡ \theta = 0$ or $sin ⁡ \theta = 1 / 2$ .

[ $sin ⁡ \theta = - 3 / 2$ is not possible]

$∴$ For, $\theta = n\pi$ the system of equations has a non-trivial solution.

We know that $\left|adj\left(adjA\right)\right| = {\left|A\right|}^{{ \left($ n - 1\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ n^{2} - 5n + 6 = 0$

Hence, the sum of all values of $n$ is equal to& $5$

$A = \left[\begin{cases}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{cases}\right]$ and $AB = BA$ (given)

$⇒ {a}_{11} + 2{a}_{12} = {a}_{11} + {a}_{21} \ldots \left(i\right)$
${a}_{11} + {a}_{12} = {a}_{12} + {a}_{22} \ldots \left(ii\right)$
${a}_{21} + 2{a}_{22} = 2{a}_{11} + {a}_{21} \ldots \left(iii\right)$
and ${a}_{21} + {a}_{22} = 2{a}_{12} + {a}_{22} \ldots \left(iv\right)$
From $\left(ii\right), {a}_{11} = {a}_{22}$
From $\left(iv\right), {a}_{21} = 2{a}_{12}$
Since, $\left|A\right| = 0 ⇒ {a}_{11}{a}_{22} - {a}_{21}{a}_{12} = 0$

$⇒ {\left({a}_{11}\right)}^{2} = 2{\left({a}_{12}\right)}^{2} ⇒ {\left(\dfrac{{a}_{11}}{{a}_{12}}\right)}^{2} = 2$

Hence, $3{\left(\dfrac{{a}_{11}}{{a}_{12}}\right)}^{4} = 12$

questions.solution:
For non-trivial solutions,
$\left|\begin{cases}a & 1 & b \\ b & 1 & a \\ a & b & ab\end{cases}\right| = 0$
$⇒ \left(a - b\right)\left(a - {b}^{2}\right) = 0$

When $a = {b}^{2},$ then $\left(4, 2\right)$
Hence, number of ordered pairs are $6$

System of equations can be written as
$\left(a - 1\right)x - y - z = 0$
$x - \left(b - 1\right)y + z = 0$
$x + y - \left(c - 1\right)z = 0$
Using Cramer's rule, for non-trivial solution $∆ = 0$
$\left|\begin{cases}\left(a - 1\right) & - 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & - \left(b - 1\right) & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & - \left(c - 1\right)\end{cases}\right| = 0$

$⇒ \left(a - 1\right)\left[bc - b - c\right] - c - b = 0$
$⇒ abc - ab - ac - bc + b + c - c - b = 0$
$⇒ ab + bc + ca = abc ⇒ \left(\dfrac{1}{a} + \dfrac{1}{b} + \dfrac{1}{c}\right) = 1$
